facts.content: The patient is now short of breath around the house.

facts.content: The primary assessment is congestive heart failure exacerbation characterized by worsening exertional and resting shortness of breath and peripheral edema with stable vital signs and examination.
facts.source_text: 1. CHF exacerbation – worsening exertional & resting SOB, peripheral edema, stable vitals/exam

facts.content: Bilateral ankle edema is assessed as likely due to fluid overload from congestive heart failure exacerbation.
facts.source_text: 2. Bilateral ankle edema – likely fluid overload from #1

facts.content: The patient is assessed as having ischemic cardiomyopathy with a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Increase furosemide to one tablet twice daily for a few days and then reassess.
facts.source_text: • ↑ Furosemide: 1 tab BID x few days, reassess

facts.content: Order full blood count, urea and electrolytes, and creatinine to assess renal function, with possible BNP testing.
Schedule an echocardiogram.
The patient was advised to monitor symptoms and call if there is deterioration.
facts.source_text: • Education: advised to monitor symptoms, call if deterioration

facts.content: The patient should have a review in one week.
The patient should seek earlier review if there is increased shortness of breath, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.
facts.source_text: • FU: review in 1 wk; sooner if ↑ SOB, CP, palpitations, dizziness
